questions.name: Linear Pairs: b, c and d from a = 120°
questions.q_figure: Two lines l and m crossing at a point, with the four angles at the crossing named a, b, c and d going round, and angle a marked 120°.
questions.s_figure: The same crossing with the four angles marked a = 120°, b = 60°, c = 120° and d = 60°.

questions.q_figure: Two lines l and m crossing at a point, with the four angles at the crossing named a, b, c and d going round it.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with the four linear pairs and the two pairs of vertically opposite angles marked in different colours.

questions.name: Perpendicular Lines: all four angles equal
questions.s_figure: Two lines crossing at right angles, with a small square at the crossing and each of the four angles marked 90°.

questions.name: Between Lines: how the segments meet
questions.q_figure: Five pairs of line segments drawn on a plane, FG with FH, AB with CD, IJ with LM, ST with UV and OP with QR, with the angle between FG and FH marked 115.3°.
questions.s_figure: The same pairs with the angle at X marked about 60° and the angle at Y marked about 80°.

questions.name: Between Lines: extending ST, UV, OP and QR
questions.q_figure: Two pairs of line segments drawn near each other, ST with UV and OP with QR, with none of them touching.
questions.s_figure: ST and UV extended beyond their ends until they meet at a point, with OP and QR extended and staying the same distance apart.

questions.name: Parallel Lines: spotting parallel pairs
questions.q_figure: A dot grid with nine line segments labelled a to i drawn between dots, some upright, some flat and some leaning.
questions.s_figure: The same grid with the pairs a, h and i; c and g; d and f; b and e each drawn in its own colour.

questions.name: Paper Folding: counting parallel lines
questions.s_figure: A square sheet after one, two, three and four horizontal folds, with the parallel lines counted as 3, 5, 9 and 17.

questions.name: Paper Folding: a fold parallel to the diagonal
questions.s_figure: A square sheet with one diagonal dashed and a second crease parallel to it, made by folding a corner onto the centre.

questions.name: Paper Folding: creases a, b, c and p, q, r
questions.q_figure: A square sheet shown in three stages: folded down the middle and opened, the two edges folded to the centre crease and opened, and two opposite corners folded onto a crease to make triangles, with the creases marked a, b, c and p, q, r.
questions.s_figure: The creased sheet with a and p, b and q, c and r each pair marked with matching arrow marks.

questions.q_figure: Two dot grids, each 3 dots across and 4 dots up: the left has a flat segment along the top row and a segment leaning up to the right, the right has a segment going down to the right across the full height and an upright segment.
questions.s_figure: The same grids with a segment drawn between dots at right angles to each given segment that fits on the grid, in a different colour, with the right angle marked.

questions.q_figure: Five red shapes on a squared grid: a pentagon with a long upright left side, a slanted four-sided shape at the top right, a six-sided shape in the middle with a long diagonal side, a right-angled triangle at the left, and a shape with a flat base and a slanted top at the bottom right.
questions.s_figure: The same five shapes with parallel sides marked by single, double and triple arrows and each right angle marked with a small square.

questions.q_figure: An empty dot grid on which to draw line segments between dots.
questions.s_figure: A dot grid with several sets of parallel segments drawn between dots, each set of a different length and direction.

questions.q_figure: A 13 by 13 dot grid with eight line segments labelled a to h drawn between dots: a and b leaning down to the right, c and d leaning up to the right, e and f steep, g gently rising and h long and gently falling.
questions.s_figure: The same grid with a segment drawn from another dot parallel to each of a to h, taking the same steps across and up or down.

questions.q_figure: Three line segments a, b and c leaning down to the right, with a steep line meeting a at one end and meeting b and c together at its other end.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with the angles between the steep line and a, c and b marked about 30°, 29° and 33°.

questions.name: Transversals: can all eight angles differ?
questions.q_figure: A line t crossing two lines l and m, with the four angles at the upper crossing numbered 1 to 4 and the four at the lower crossing numbered 5 to 8, each set going round from the top left.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with the vertically opposite pairs 1 and 3, 2 and 4, 5 and 7, 6 and 8 marked in matching colours.

questions.name: Corresponding Angles: drawing a parallel line
questions.q_figure: A line l and a transversal t crossing at a point X, with the angle a between them marked 60° and a point Y marked on t.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with a line m drawn through Y so that the angle b at Y is 60°, and l and m shown parallel with arrow marks.

questions.name: Set Square: lines along the upright edge
questions.q_figure: A line l drawn along a ruler, with a set square beside it and two lines drawn along its upright edge at two positions.
questions.s_figure: The two drawn lines with arrow marks and the 90° angle marked where each meets l.

questions.name: Set Square: the long side at 45°
questions.q_figure: A line l drawn along a ruler, with a 45° set square beside it whose long side slopes across l, and two lines drawn along that long side at two positions.
questions.s_figure: The two drawn lines with arrow marks and the 45° angle marked where each meets l.

questions.q_figure: A line l with a point A marked above it.
questions.s_figure: The line through A drawn parallel to l, with the ruler and set square placed as used.

questions.name: Parallel Lines by Folding: through the point A
questions.q_figure: A rectangular sheet with a dashed crease l across it and a point A marked above l.
questions.s_figure: The sheet with a crease t through A at right angles to l and a second crease m through A at right angles to t, with both right angles marked.

questions.name: Alternate Angles: f is 120°, find d
questions.q_figure: Two parallel lines l and m with arrow marks cut by a transversal t, the angles at the upper crossing named a and b on top and d and c below them, those at the lower crossing named e and f on top and h and g below them, and f marked 120°.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with b = 120° marked as the corresponding angle of f and d = 120° marked as the vertically opposite angle of b.

questions.name: Example 1: all angles from 135°
questions.q_figure: Two parallel lines l and m cut by a transversal t, with the angles numbered 1 to 4 at the crossing with l and 5 to 8 at the crossing with m, the same corners in the same order, and angle 6 marked 135°.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with angles 2, 4, 6 and 8 marked 135° and angles 1, 3, 5 and 7 marked 45°.

questions.name: Example 2: are l and m parallel?
questions.q_figure: Two lines l and m cut by a transversal t, the angles at the upper crossing named a and b on top and d and c below them, those at the lower crossing named e and f on top and h and g below them, with a marked 120° and f marked 70°.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with b marked 60° next to a and set beside f = 70° as a pair of corresponding angles that differ.

questions.name: Example 3: angle 6 from angle 3
questions.q_figure: Two parallel lines l and m cut by a transversal t, with the angles at the upper crossing numbered 1 to 4 and those at the lower crossing numbered 5 to 8 going round from the top left, and angle 3 marked 50°.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with angle 2 marked 130° and angle 6 marked 130°, and angles 3 and 6 shown as interior angles on the same side.

questions.name: Example 4: finding CAB, ABC and BCD
questions.q_figure: A four-sided figure ABCD with AB parallel to CD and AD parallel to BC marked by arrows, the line AC drawn inside it, angle DAC marked 65° and angle ADC marked 60°.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with angle DAB marked 120°, angle CAB 55°, angle ABC 60° and angle BCD 120°.

questions.q_figure: Ten small figures labelled a to j, each with two or three parallel lines marked by arrows and crossed by a line, with some angles marked in degrees and the angle to find marked with its letter.
questions.s_figure: Each figure with its letter filled in: a = 48°, b = 52°, c = 81°, d = 99°, e = 69°, f = 48°, g = 122°, h = 75°, i = 54°, j = 97°.

questions.q_figure: Four figures (i) to (iv) of parallel lines crossed by a line, with 42° and 100° in the first, 62° in the second, 110° and 35° in the third, and 67° beside a right angle in the fourth, and the angle a marked in each.
questions.s_figure: Each figure with a filled in: 138°, 118°, 105° and 23°.

questions.q_figure: Two figures: the first has two parallel lines crossed by a slanted line and by an upright line with a right angle marked, with 65° and the angles x and y marked; the second has two parallel lines crossed by two lines that meet on the upper one, with 53°, 78° and the angle x marked.
questions.s_figure: Each figure with the angles filled in: x = 25° and y = 155° in the first, x = 25° in the second.

questions.q_figure: Two parallel lines, the upper through I, K, B and A and the lower through G, E and D, crossed by a line through J, K, E and F and by a line through C, B, E and H, with angle IKJ marked 78° and angle ABC marked 45°.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with angle GEH marked 45°, angle HEF marked 57° and angle FED marked 78°.

questions.q_figure: Three upright parallel lines AB, CD and EF, crossed along the top by the horizontal line ACE and by a slanted line from B through D to E, with angle BEF marked 55° and the angles x at B and y at D marked.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with x and y both marked 125°.

questions.q_figure: Two upright parallel lines LM and PQ joined by a zigzag path M, N, O, P, with 40° marked at M, 96° at N, 52° at P and the angle a marked at O.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with a line through N and a line through O drawn parallel to LM and PQ, and the angle NOP marked 108°.
